transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-03-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jonas Reed (Redwood SE); Sofia Alvarez (Tethys); Ravi Menon (Tethys); Diane Cho (Tethys)

Optional autogenerated sections:
- Topics: partner GTM, technical fit, pilot scope
- Action items: listed below

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood partnerships team. Uh, quick round of intros?
[00:10] Sofia Alvarez: Hi, Sofia here, Head of Partnerships at Tethys. We focus on integrating cloud GPU capacity into managed SI offerings, so we resell + manage for enterprise.
[00:19] Ravi Menon: Ravi, lead cloud architect. We'll be responsible for the technical validation and ops side.
[00:24] Diane Cho: Diane, biz dev — I'm here to map channel motions and commercials.
[00:29] Jonas Reed: Jonas, SE, Redwood. I'll dig into perf, deploy modes, and what a POC would look like.
[00:35] Maya Patel: Great. High level — today's goal is to see whether there's a clean channel + SI fit: whether Tethys can package Redwood's inference runtime and Dedicated/Private options into your managed offering.
[00:46] Sofia Alvarez: Yes. A couple things — our customers care about latency for chat apps and throughput for embedding pipelines. We also need to understand margining and how we can white-label or resell.
[00:58] Jonas Reed: Understood. Just to frame technical options quickly: Redwood offers Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated customers. Each has tradeoffs — Hosted is easiest but less isolated; Private gives you full network control but longer lead time.
[01:14] Ravi Menon: On privacy — we have a few customers in finance and healthcare. They require customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and usually a VPC peering option. Can Redwood support customer KMS and HSM integrations?
[01:28] Maya Patel: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS and support HSM-based key wraps for Private deployments; audit logs and SSO/SAML are supported. We can share the security checklist.
[01:36] Diane Cho: For the reseller economics, do you have a partner margin sheet or channel pricing?
[01:42] Maya Patel: We do — I'll share the one-pager and a suggested margin structure. Typical is a reseller discount on usage + fixed fee for Dedicated commitments. We can also support marketplace listings if that's part of the go-to-market.
[01:55] Sofia Alvarez: Marketplace would be helpful. For Dedicated, how does autoscaling and burst capacity work? Our customers sometimes have spiky loads.
[02:04] Jonas Reed: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst into spare capacity tiers. We also have routing policies that can fall back to cheaper variants — e.g., quantized models — when capacity constrains. Note: for tight latency SLOs we tend to pin to guaranteed capacity.
[02:19] Sofia Alvarez: Okay. On the integration side — do you expose an SDK or is it just REST? Our engineering teams usually want an SDK and a lightweight operator integration for deployment.
[02:28] Jonas Reed: We have a REST API + SDKs. For Private, we provide a helm chart and an operator for on-prem installs; for VPC we do a customer-managed control plane. There might be some missing words in the transcript — the ops artifact is basically a deploy pack with kube manifests.
[02:45] Ravi Menon: Sounds promising. For the POC, we want to run a sample workload: 50 QPS for chat with 32-token avg latencies and a weekly batch of 2 million embeddings. Can Redwood give us cost/latency projections for that?
[02:58] Jonas Reed: Yes. We can run a short benchmark — two paths: lightweight hosted baseline (fastest to start) and a Dedicated profile to show predictable throughput and unit economics. We'll need your prompt/embedding input and sequence length distribution to model cost.
[03:13] Diane Cho: Timeline-wise, we typically want a demo to our sales engineering, then an internal pilot with 2 target customers over 6–8 weeks. Is that a feasible pilot window?
[03:24] Maya Patel: Absolutely feasible. We usually do a 4–8 week pilot depending on access to data and environment. If we start with hosted, it's quicker. For Private it adds provisioning lead time.
[03:33] Sofia Alvarez: One question: can Redwood support white-labeling the UI or at least allow us to own the billing of end customers? Some of our deals require billing under our contract.
[03:43] Maya Patel: We can support partner billing via reseller arrangements and marketplace flows; white-label UI is trickier on hosted but for Dedicated/Private you can host your own control plane and integrate our runtime under your branding. We'll need legal to sign off on reseller terms.
[03:55] Ravi Menon: On networking, what does VPC peering look like? Do you do transit VPC or direct peering? We need to document the exact traffic flow and egress implications for our customers.
[04:06] Jonas Reed: For VPC/private we support direct VPC peering and private link equivalents depending on cloud provider. We'll provide a network topology diagram and egress guidelines — there's some variability by region and provider.
[04:18] Sofia Alvarez: Do you have any channel co-sell incentives or lead credits?
[04:22] Maya Patel: Yes, we have lead credits and co-sell arrangements; we also provide joint marketing support for priority partners. We'll include GTM enablement materials in the partner packet.
[04:32] Diane Cho: Any limitations on model catalog? We often onboard customers wanting Llama variants and some proprietary small models.
[04:38] Jonas Reed: We support a curated model catalog and can onboard partner-requested models. For private/pinned models there's a validation phase around licensing and compatibility. Also note: in transcript the product name Redwood Optimize got spelled as 'Redwood Optimise' earlier in doc, minor discrepancy.
[04:56] Maya Patel: Let's talk about success criteria for a pilot: SLOs, cost targets, and customer acceptance. Typical metrics: 95th percentile latency under X ms, embedding cost per 1k under Y dollars, and integration work less than Z engineering-weeks.
[05:10] Ravi Menon: Those metrics are fine; we will provide a target customer and sample telemetry to measure. Also need to check SOC2/ISO reports; can you share SOC2 Type II?
[05:20] Maya Patel: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO summaries available. We'll share redacted reports under an NDA.
[05:26] Sofia Alvarez: Good. On board ops: what's the provisioning time for a Private deployment in our EU region? Our customers need EU data residency.
[05:36] Jonas Reed: For Private VPC in EU, provisioning is typically 2–4 weeks depending on customer infra readiness and KMS/HSM setup. Hosted in an EU region is immediate, but note hosted data residency guarantees vary by contract.
[05:50] Diane Cho: Commercially, if we commit to a Dedicated reserve on behalf of a customer, can Tethys get a volume discount?
[05:57] Maya Patel: Yes, Partner/Reseller volume discounts can be structured as an addendum to the Dedicated contract. We'll outline tiers in the margin sheet.
[06:05] Ravi Menon: A technical nit: KV cache behavior — if we run large context chains, how does Redwood handle KV eviction and batching? We've had trouble with other systems reloading the kv too often.
[06:14] Jonas Reed: Good question. Our runtime does continuous batching and manages KV cache across requests; behavior depends on sequence length distribution and model variant. We have caching strategies and an option for a sticky session pin to keep KV warm for certain flows. I'll share a short technical note on cache heuristics.
[06:30] Sofia Alvarez: Any constraints on model quantization for specific accuracy needs? Some customers need high fidelity for legal text generation.
[06:36] Jonas Reed: Right — quantization reduces memory and cost but can affect output quality. We recommend A/B testing with your prompt sets; Redwood Optimize provides recommended quantization profiles per workload. We'll include that in the perf deliverable.
[06:48] Maya Patel: Ok, let's recap next steps (quick): Maya share partner packet and margin sheet; Jonas run baseline and share perf notes; Ravi provide sample workload and residency constraints; Sofia coordinate executive sync. Any other asks?
[07:01] Diane Cho: Please include a sample SLA for Dedicated + support tiers.
[07:05] Maya Patel: Will do.
[07:08] Sofia Alvarez: Also, if possible, include an example reseller contract term sheet.
[07:12] Maya Patel: We'll include a term sheet template.
[07:15] Jonas Reed: I'll start a lightweight bench run on hosted using your embeddings and chat traces once Ravi shares. Expect initial numbers in 5 business days.
[07:25] Ravi Menon: Sounds good. One minor point: any known outages or fallbacks for regional capacity? Customers fear sudden capacity loss.
[07:33] Maya Patel: We have routing and fallback policies — we can route to model variants or alternate regions, and Dedicated has SLA-backed capacity. We'll include our fallback playbook.
[07:42] Diane Cho: Great. That covers most things. Thanks all.
[07:46] Maya Patel: Thank you — Maya to follow up with materials.
[07:50] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks. We'll aim to share sample by end of week.

(Transcript contains occasional transcription noise and mislabels; some product names spelled slightly differently in conversation.)
